title: Hit-recoil + spring-sway animation systems (the two unshipped pieces of GDP-2026-05-20-009)
intent: GDP-2026-05-20-009 (full six animation systems pack) is still pending. But four of the six are already partially or fully shipped after S102 + S103: idle-bob ✅ (S101 stub, kept in S102), walk-cycle ✅ (S103 PROCBOMBER-WALK-CYCLE-PLUS — shoulders + hips + knees + elbows), bomb-place-reach ✅ partial (S103 IK + 'reach' kind exists; only the wiring to PlaceBombRequest is missing), slapstick-death ✅ (S100 KABOOM-SLAPSTICK-DEATH). Two of the six are NOT YET TOUCHED: hit-recoil (torso flinch on blast hit) and spring-sway (secondary motion on soft-attached accessories). This story finishes the pack by adding exactly those two systems, plus wiring the reach IK system to the actual PlaceBombRequest event (instead of the bench dropdown). After this lands, GDP-2026-05-20-009 is fully covered and that older proposal can be marked superseded.
rationale: Source: original proposal GDP-2026-05-20-009 (still pending) reframed against shipped reality. The 6-systems-as-one-story scope made sense when nothing had shipped; it doesn't make sense to re-promote that as-is when ~70% of the work has already landed in different stories. This re-frame is the minimum-cost path to closing the original intent: two new systems + one trivial wiring change, instead of rewriting four already-working systems. Also bundles in the spring-sway dependency on accessories (GDP-2026-05-22-003): without accessories there are no soft-attached nodes for spring-sway to operate on — so this story is sequenced AFTER accessories.
acceptanceHints: Depends on GDP-2026-05-22-002 (migration — animation systems live in kaboom-crew side after that lands) AND GDP-2026-05-22-003 (accessories — spring-sway operates on soft-attached accessory nodes).
PART A — Hit-recoil system (NEW):

examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/anim/hit-recoil-system.ts: on a BlastEvent that overlaps a bomber's grid cell, schedule a Tween on the bomber's torso entity Transform.rotation.x by -8 degrees (pitch back) over 0.10 s, then return to 0 over 0.18 s. Total ~0.28 s.

Hit-recoil is independent of slapstick-death (the existing root-Transform death tween from S100). When a blast is LETHAL, both tweens fire — hit-recoil on the torso + death on the root. The combination is fine; both write different Transform fields on different entities (torso = child, root = parent).
Hit-recoil also fires for NON-lethal hits — useful for future Shield power-up scenarios where a blast hits but doesn't kill. Currently every blast is lethal; the system is forward-compatible.

Unit tests: hit on dead bomber → no tween (alive=false guard), hit on alive bomber → torso pitch oscillates and returns to 0 within budget, two rapid blasts → tween restarts cleanly (no leaked tween references).
PART B — Spring-sway system (NEW):

examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/anim/spring-sway-system.ts: generic two-tap spring on any entity carrying the `SoftAttached` component (added to schema in GDP-2026-05-22-003). The system reads the entity's parent Transform's angular velocity over the last few fixedUpdate frames and applies an inverse spring-damper to the entity's local rotation.

Spring parameters: k = 18 (stiffness), damping = 0.4. These produce a settling within ~6 fixedUpdate ticks at AGF's default tick rate — visually a soft wobble, not a slow drift. Hardcoded constants; future tuning via SoftAttached.k / SoftAttached.damping (optional schema fields).

ONE system covers EVERY soft-attached node across EVERY character. No per-character animation state — the system is stateless aside from the angular-velocity ring buffer it keeps per entity (small fixed cost).
Soft-attached entities (from accessory tagging in GDP-003 of this batch): antenna cylinders + antenna tips, fin meshes. Cap + visor + backpack are NOT soft-attached — they're rigid.

Unit tests: zero parent motion → soft-attached entity stays at rest, sudden parent rotation → soft-attached entity overshoots then settles within ~6 ticks (assert peak overshoot and settle time numerically).
PART C — Bomb-place IK wiring (CHANGE):

Currently the bench's 'reach' animation kind drives the IK solver against a hardcoded demo target. After this story lands, the kaboom-crew side's bomb-place-animation-system.ts (created during GDP-2026-05-22-002 migration) subscribes to `PlaceBombRequest`. On a place-request, the system:
1. Picks the closer arm (shoulder-to-bomb-cell distance).
2. Sets the IK target to the bomb cell's centre in shoulder-local space (uses the existing solveTwoBoneIk from S103).
3. Tweens the arm to that target over 0.18 s ease-out, holds 0.05 s, returns to the rest pose over 0.12 s.

The bench's 'reach' dropdown stays as a debug visualisation — it sets a demo target without a PlaceBombRequest. Bench dropdown and production triggering are different code paths, both calling the same IK solver.
Unit test: PlaceBombRequest → animation system writes shoulder + elbow rotations toward the bomb cell within one fixedUpdate; tween completes within budget; arm returns to rest pose afterward.

Pack-completion verification: after this story lands, all six animations from GDP-2026-05-20-009 are real. Update GDP-2026-05-20-009's archive entry (or the relevant epic note) to mark it superseded by the combination [S100 slapstick-death, S101 idle-bob stub, S102 walk-cycle, S103 walk-cycle-plus + IK + reach, GDP-2026-05-22-002 migration, this story].

Performance: spring-sway is the only system with per-entity state. At 4 bombers × 3 soft-attached nodes each = 12 spring entities. Ring buffer per entity = ~8 floats. Negligible memory; negligible per-tick cost.

Bench presence: hit-recoil and spring-sway can be previewed in the bench too — add a 'hit-recoil' dropdown option (manually triggers the tween on the bench bomber) and a 'sway-test' option that briefly rotates the bomber root so soft-attached accessories visibly sway. Both are debug-only.

Out of scope (explicit): foot-plant during walk-cycle (deferred S104 per S103 notes — depends on hip-Y compensation), bomb-throw animation (no Throw Glove yet), kick contact animation (no special anim for kick in MVP — bomber stride keeps going), victory dance (would tie into GDP-2026-05-20-010 vocal synth victory slot — separate story when both land), facial expressions (no face primitives in the recipe).
